items.q: Why do shortlisted candidates only seem lucky?
items.a: Vinh defines luck as **preparation meeting opportunity**. Shortlisted people prepared answers for questions they already knew were coming — they didn't get lucky.

items.q: If the top interview questions are predictable, why do candidates still fail?
items.a: Vinh sourced a **top 10 list** from recruiter friend Jared (Australia). Most people still **wing answers** they know will be asked — especially **"tell us about yourself,"** which is almost always first.

Craft a prepared **2–3 minute origin story** — often a **childhood or formative memory** — that reveals character, builds rapport, and **links explicitly to the role**. Adjectives like "integrity, honesty, punctuality" don't connect; stories do.

items.q: How does Vinh's Apple Head of Innovation demo work?
items.a: He improvises: 13-year-old wants love → dad says **"no money, no honey"** → discovers eBay → resells MP3 players → lifelong **early-adopter pattern** (Vision Pro, AI music, iPhone launch lines) → therefore fits **innovation leadership**. The story maps directly to the job.

items.q: How do you keep the origin story from feeling like a monologue?
items.a: Make it **conversational** — ask the interviewer questions mid-story, use humor, and shift the room from interrogation to **dialogue**.

items.q: What happens chemically after a few minutes of storytelling?
items.a: Storytelling triggers **dopamine, endorphins, and oxytocin**. After ~**3 minutes**, Vinh says the interviewer starts treating you as a **friend**, not a faceless candidate — differentiating you from hundreds who only list traits.
